The joint stands on the discharge side of the circuit served by the absorber, where the lean solvent pump holds the pressure the gasket has to seal against, so the temperature at the joint follows the duty of the absorber rather than the nameplate condition of the compressor casing alone.

The thickness also governs how the joint is made up, since the gasket is compressed between faces whose separation the wall and the flange together determine, and the joint so formed is the part of the casing that the comparison below has to serve.
